[[File:SD line vs regression line.png|thumb|Plot of the standard deviation line (SD line), dashed, and the regression line, solid, for a scatter diagram of 20 points.]]
In [[statistics]], the '''standard deviation line''' (or SD line) marks points on a [[scatter plot]] that are an equal number of [[standard deviation]]s away from the average in each dimension. For example, in a 2-dimensional scatter diagram with variables <math>x</math> and <math>y</math>, points that are 1 standard deviation away from the mean of <math>x</math> and also 1 standard deviation away from the mean of <math>y</math> are on the SD line.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Freedman |first=David |title=Statistics |date=1998 |publisher=W.W. Norton |others=Robert Pisani, Roger Purves |isbn=0-393-97083-3 |edition=3rd |location=New York |oclc=36922529}}</ref> The SD line is a useful visual tool since points in a scatter diagram tend to cluster around it,<ref name=":0" /> more or less tightly depending on their [[correlation]].

== Properties ==

=== Relation to regression line ===
The SD line goes through the point of averages and has a slope of <math>\frac{\sigma_y}{\sigma_x} </math> when the correlation between <math>x</math> and <math>y</math> is positive, and <math>-\frac{\sigma_y}{\sigma_x}</math> when the correlation is negative.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Stark |title=Regression |url=https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~stark/SticiGui/Text/regression.htm |access-date=2022-11-12 |website=www.stat.berkeley.edu}}</ref> Unlike the [[regression line]], the SD line does not take into account the relationship between <math>x</math> and <math>y</math>.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cochran |title=Regression |url=http://www.stat.ucla.edu/~cochran/stat10/winter/lectures/lect16.html |access-date=2022-11-12 |website=www.stat.ucla.edu}}</ref> The slope of the SD line is related to that of the regression line by <math>a = r \frac{\sigma_y}{\sigma_x}</math> where <math>a</math> is the slope of the regression line, <math>r</math> is the [[correlation coefficient]], and <math>\frac{\sigma_y}{\sigma_x}</math> is the magnitude of the slope of the SD line.<ref name=":1" />

=== Typical distance of points to SD line ===
The [[root mean square]] vertical distance of points from the SD line is <math>\sqrt{2(1 - |r|)} \times\sigma_y</math>.<ref name=":0" /> This gives an idea of the spread of points around the SD line.
